newsitem.title: UK: Guinness exec urges consumer understanding.
newsitem.headline: Guinness exec urges consumer understanding.

text.p: Understanding consumers, including being attuned to trendsetters and having insight into one's owns customers, is the key to innovation profitable growth, Tony Greener, chairman of Guinness Plc, said on Wednesday.
"We believe that what opens the door to innovation -- innovation that can lead to superior brand building -- is better consumer understanding," Greener told the Marketing Society annual conference.
Greener cited NIKE Inc, the athletic footwear and apparel company, as a prime example of a company built on understanding the consumer.

"They rely on the best athletes in each sport, to get to the consumer in the street and influence the base of the pyramid," Greener said. "To break into a new sport, their managers will spend a whole week in isolation practising the sport and talking to some of the world's best athletes in that discipline."

Guinness' success in exporting themed Irish pubs around the world -- the company has opened 1,000 Irish pubs in partnerships with local entrepreneurs -- reflects the idea of one insightful Guinness manager in Ireland who had a close understanding of pub owners and patrons, Greener said.

"The challenge for many companies where managers are not themselves regular consumers, day in day out, is to bridge the gap to the regular consumer," he said. "In some situations we have found it is almost necessary to 'force' management in front of consumers, because in reality there is no substitute for the touch and feel."
